claim: If a cluster with replicas has Multi-AZ enabled and the primary fails, the primary fails over to a read replica; because replicas are updated asynchronously, some data may be lost. For clusters with durability enabled, data is persisted in a Multi-AZ transactional log: with synchronous writes no acknowledged data is lost during failover, and with asynchronous writes up to 10 seconds of data may be lost in case of a failure.

evidence.quote: If the cluster with replicas has Multi-AZ enabled and the primary node fails, the primary fails over to a read replica. Because the data is updated on the replica nodes asynchronously, there may be some data loss due to latency in updating the replica nodes.

For clusters with durability enabled, data is persisted in a Multi-AZ transactional log and can be recovered even if all nodes fail. With synchronous writes, no acknowledged data is lost during failover. With asynchronous writes, up to 10 seconds of data may be lost in case of a failure.
